rv.q: Butler conveys Hamer’s story with great clarity and power.
Butler's performance, with all of its love and its pain, does her subject proud.
This is a tour de force one-woman performance, in this writer's view.
Butler brings vibrantly, lovingly to life in a turn as irrepressible as it is coherent and credible.
This is a performance that truly hits home and shouldn’t be missed.

It also would be difficult to think of anyone more ideally suited to meeting this challenge than Chicago actress and singer E. Faye Butler, who has been a theatrical groundbreaker herself for many years.
"Fannie" is a "MUST SEE" for any history buff and for those who lean towards getting involved in the political scene.

Director Henry Godinez tastefully weaves together civil rights images and stylized movement, while music director Felton Offard constructs a score of black spirituals to elevate this hero’s journey to epic proportions.
Ultimately, Fannie is a play about the past that serves as a call to action for the present.

cn.t: E. Faye Butler delivers a powerhouse performance that electrifies critics in this one-woman show chronicling civil rights icon Fannie Lou Hamer, with reviewers praising the energy, emotion, and vocal prowess that brings this vital story to life.
